image_description: A close-up, low-angle photograph of a fossilized Triceratops skull mounted in a museum setting. The image focuses on the massive bony frill and the base of the horns. Two large brow horns are visible projecting upwards, though their tips are cropped out of the frame. The nasal horn area is partially visible but appears structurally anomalous, potentially fused with the brow horn base or exhibiting impossible fenestration (holes) for a solid-bone specimen. The bone texture shows cracks and fossilization patterns but also areas of smudging or inconsistent grain. In the background, there is a ceiling light fixture and parts of other skeletal mounts.
